record.paper_title: Open Problems in Human Trait Genetics
record.original_question: How much do underrepresented forms of genetic variation—such as sex chromosomes, mitochondrial DNA, structural and copy-number variants, repetitive regions, phasing, mosaicism, and alternatives to representing genomes as deviations from one reference genome—contribute to complex traits and missing heritability, and how should human genetic studies measure and model them?

evidence.quote: there are certain types of genetic variation that are systematically underrepresented, or altogether absent, from contemporary genetic studies (open problem #5: non-standard genetic variation).

Whether this is an anecdotal phenomenon or an important aspect of human genetics still remains to be determined. Should mosaicism be taken into account in genetic studies, or is it better treated as yet another non-genetic factor (like other omics and environmental effects)?
The overall contribution of unaccounted genetic variation to heritability, and whether this is a major source of missing heritability, is yet to be determined.

artifact.status_search_result: The contribution of non-standard genetic variation (sex chromosomes, mtDNA, structural/copy-number variants, repeats, phasing, mosaicism, pangenome-level variation) to complex-trait heritability remains an active and unresolved area. Recent large-scale efforts (e.g., the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, long-read sequencing in UK Biobank/All of Us, and tandem-repeat and SV association studies through 2024–2025) have begun quantifying contributions of individual classes (notably tandem repeats and SVs), but no comprehensive accounting of their joint contribution to missing heritability or a unified modeling framework has been established.

status_evidence.title: Human Pangenome Reference Consortium
status_evidence.snippet: The HPRC is building a pangenome reference to capture variation missed by a single linear reference, with ongoing releases as of 2024–2025.
status_evidence.claim: Pangenome-based representation of human genomes is still an active research effort, indicating non-reference variation is not yet routinely modeled in heritability studies.

status_evidence.title: Polymorphic tandem repeats contribute to complex traits (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent studies estimate substantial trait variance explained by tandem repeats beyond SNPs, but only for selected traits.
status_evidence.claim: Quantification of underrepresented variation classes is partial and ongoing, not comprehensive.
